scope: Limited manual inspection of 16 named views from the forward 0.5% body-height socket trial against the preserved taper. No actual game-animation or dressed qualification.
observations: The forward socket shift lowers 90-degree shoulder intersections from 131/81 to 63/42 with the same skin weights. All non-shoulder bend counts remain unchanged, and all 16 poses retain zero severe-stretch edges.
Paired oblique and selected side views show no gross detached or separated shoulder. The rounded/compressed shoulder transition remains; these views do not establish acceptable deep-flexion shape.

Selected front, side, back and skeleton bind views preserve the overall silhouette and supported feet. Selected 45-degree front views show the intended bent arm. The 90-degree front close views are partially occluded by the forearm/hand, so they cannot independently clear the armpit.
Both inspected 90-degree hip close views retain the deep flexion crease. Hip contacts remain 255/133; this shoulder-only study does not repair them.

Both exact diagnostic exports reproduce all 16 stored counts; 68 screenshots rendered without browser errors. Only the 16 listed images were manually assessed, and the clips are diagnostics rather than qualified game animations.
decision: Retain as a promising numerical diagnostic, without replacing the immutable taper baseline or clearing the deformation gate. Next test a separately frozen combined outward/forward placement within the same 1% displacement cap, with weights and axes fixed; map residual contacts before any targeted surface correction.
